answers.primary: A subagent (built-in general-purpose or a small custom test-runner definition) that runs the integration suite in its own context window and returns only the failing tests with their error messages; this is the documented isolate-high-volume-operations pattern for subagents.
answers.rejected_alternative: A skill: skills run in the main conversation context, so the thousands of log lines would land in the working conversation, which is exactly what must not happen.
answers.enforcement_owner: Split: the harness owns the isolation, because the suite's raw output physically accumulates in the subagent's separate transcript and never enters the main window; the model owns choosing to delegate and the fidelity of the summary it sends back.
answers.context_boundary: The suite executes inside the subagent's own context window; only Claude's delegation prompt crosses in, and only the final report of failing tests plus errors crosses back. The raw output is discarded with the subagent's context and its transcript is cleaned up after the retention period.
answers.lifecycle: Spawned per delegation through the Agent tool, either automatically when the task matches the subagent's description or on explicit request or @-mention; it works independently, returns one report, and the instance ends. Each new invocation starts a fresh instance.
answers.failure_mode: Advisory at the delegation step: Claude may fail to delegate and run the suite inline, and a chatty subagent can still return a verbose report that consumes main context. Once delegated the raw logs cannot leak into the main window, but anything the summary omits is lost unless the subagent is resumed.
answers.version_caveat: As of v2.1.198 subagents run in the background by default, where they get a reduced built-in tool set; Claude runs one in the foreground only when it needs the result before continuing.

enforcement_owner.quote: the subagent does that work in its own context and returns only the summary

lifecycle.quote: When Claude encounters a task that matches a subagent's description, it delegates to that subagent, which works independently and returns results.

failure_mode.quote: Running many subagents that each return detailed results can consume significant context.

version_caveat.quote: As of v2.1.198, subagents run in the background by default.

answers.primary: A custom subagent whose frontmatter `tools` field is an allowlist of read-only tools (tools: Read, Grep, Glob), deliberately excluding Write, Edit, Bash, and PowerShell so there is no shell escape; the harness never offers the excluded tools to the worker.
answers.rejected_alternative: Prompt-level restriction (a system prompt or CLAUDE.md rule saying do not modify files): it is advisory text the model can ignore mid-task, and the scenario explicitly requires the constraint to hold no matter what the instructions or the model decide.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: tools absent from the resolved allowlist are simply not in the subagent's tool pool, so the restriction holds regardless of the model's behavior or instructions.
answers.context_boundary: The reviewer runs in its own context window with fresh context; the delegation prompt and CLAUDE.md cross in, only its review report crosses back, and it never sees the main conversation history.
answers.lifecycle: The definition lives in .claude/agents/ (or ~/.claude/agents/) and is watched for live edits; a fresh instance is created for each delegation and ends when it returns its report.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for tool access but fails open on misconfiguration: omitting the `tools` field inherits every tool available to subagents, and adding Bash would reopen file modification through the shell. A tools list that resolves to nothing makes the launch fail with an error naming the entries.
answers.version_caveat: Zero-tool protection is version-gated: on v2.1.208 and later Claude Code refuses to launch a subagent whose tools list resolves to nothing, while earlier versions launched it with no tools.

enforcement_owner.quote: To restrict tools, use the `tools` field as an allowlist or the `disallowedTools` field as a denylist.

lifecycle.quote: Each subagent invocation creates a new instance with fresh context.

failure_mode.quote: Inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted.

version_caveat.quote: Before v2.1.208, that subagent launched with no tools and could return an empty or confusing result.

answers.primary: The built-in /btw side-question command (interactive-mode harness feature): nothing needs to be built. It has full visibility into the current conversation, needs no tools, and both question and answer live in a dismissible overlay that never enters conversation history.
answers.rejected_alternative: A subagent: it is the documented inverse of this need, starting with an empty context so it cannot draw on the discussion so far, and its result would be appended to the conversation, consuming history.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: the ephemerality (overlay only, never written to history) and the no-tool-access constraint are properties of the /btw mechanism itself, not model compliance.
answers.context_boundary: The side question is answered against the parent conversation's full context, reusing its prompt cache; nothing crosses back into the transcript, and the answer exists only in the overlay until dismissed.
answers.lifecycle: Runs when you type /btw <question>, even while Claude is processing a turn; it produces a single response with no follow-up turns, and the overlay is dismissed with Space, Enter, or Escape. Earlier exchanges stay reviewable in the overlay until cleared.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed on tools: it cannot read files, run commands, or search, so a question needing new evidence gets an answer limited to what is already in context; and with no follow-up turns, continuing the thread requires forking it into a new session with `f`.
answers.version_caveat: Overlay reopen behavior is version-gated: v2.1.212 added running /btw with no question to reopen the most recent exchange, and stepping through earlier answers with Left/Right requires v2.1.187 or later.

enforcement_owner.quote: The question and answer are ephemeral: they appear in a dismissible overlay and never enter the conversation history.

lifecycle.quote: there are no follow-up turns in the overlay. To continue the thread, fork it into its own session with `f`.

failure_mode.quote: side questions answer only from what is already in context. Claude can't read files, run commands, or search when answering a side question.

version_caveat.quote: Before v2.1.212, `/btw` without a question printed a usage message instead.

answers.primary: A conversation fork started with /subtask (a forked subagent): it inherits the entire two-hour conversation, so the helper starts with every finding, ruled-out hypothesis, config quirk, and stack trace already in context, drafts the regression tests in the background, and returns only its result while you keep working on the fix.
answers.rejected_alternative: A named/custom subagent: it starts from a fresh context, so all the accumulated debugging context would have to be re-summarized into a delegation prompt, which is precisely the re-explaining the user wants to avoid.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: inheriting the full transcript, system prompt, and tools is structural to the fork mechanism, and its tool calls are kept out of the main window by the harness; the quality of the drafted tests is the model's responsibility.
answers.context_boundary: The fork receives a snapshot of the entire main-session context as of the moment it spawns and shares the parent's prompt cache; its own tool calls stay in its transcript, and only the final result comes back as a message in the main conversation.
answers.lifecycle: Started by typing /subtask <task> (or by Claude requesting the fork subagent type where fork mode is enabled); it runs in the background, can be watched and steered from the panel below the prompt, and ends when its result is delivered.
answers.failure_mode: The inherited context is frozen at spawn time, so fixes you make afterward are invisible to the fork and its drafted tests can go stale against the moving code; a fork also cannot spawn further forks. This is a delegation convenience, not an enforcement mechanism, so nothing fails closed.
answers.version_caveat: The /subtask command requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later; before that the forked-subagent command was /fork, and letting Claude itself spawn forks remains experimental under staged rollout with the CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT variable as the explicit override.

enforcement_owner.quote: A fork is a subagent that inherits the entire conversation so far instead of starting fresh.

lifecycle.quote: The fork appears in a panel below your prompt and runs in the background while you keep working. When it finishes, its result arrives as a message in your main conversation.

failure_mode.quote: A fork inherits everything the main session has at the moment it spawns.

version_caveat.quote: Run a forked subagent with `/subtask`, which requires Claude Code v2.1.212 or later.

answers.primary: A skill with `context: fork` and `agent: Explore` (the documented pr-summary pattern): the team triggers it by name with /skill-name, the written procedure in SKILL.md becomes the prompt driving an isolated subagent, all intermediate file reads and command output stay in that fork's context, and Explore's read-only tool set (Write and Edit denied) enforces read-only execution.
answers.rejected_alternative: A custom subagent: it also gives isolation and read-only tools, but it is invoked through Claude's delegation, with Claude writing the task prompt each time, whereas the skill keeps the team's written multi-step procedure verbatim and gives the exact by-name /trigger the team already uses.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: it creates the isolated fork context and withholds Write/Edit from the Explore agent type; only faithful execution of the procedure's steps inside the fork belongs to the model.
answers.context_boundary: A new isolated context is created per invocation; the rendered SKILL.md content (including any dynamic-context command output) crosses in as the subagent's prompt, and only the summarized result returns to the invoking conversation. None of the intermediate reads land in the invoking context.
answers.lifecycle: Runs when a user types /skill-name (or when Claude invokes it, unless disable-model-invocation is set); by default the forked subagent runs in the background and its result arrives when it completes, ending the instance.
answers.failure_mode: A skill body that contains guidelines without an explicit task makes the fork return nothing useful; and because a backgrounded fork runs with the narrower background subagent tool set, a procedure step that depends on an excluded tool fails unless background: false is set. The read-only constraint itself fails closed via the Explore tool set.
answers.version_caveat: The `background: false` frontmatter escape requires Claude Code v2.1.218 or later; on earlier versions forked skills always blocked the invoking turn until they finished.

enforcement_owner.quote: read-only tools; Write and Edit are denied

lifecycle.quote: Add `context: fork` to your frontmatter when you want a skill to run in isolation. The skill content becomes the prompt that drives the subagent.

failure_mode.quote: the subagent receives the guidelines but no actionable prompt, and returns without meaningful output

version_caveat.quote: Before v2.1.218, forked skills always blocked the turn until they finished.

answers.primary: A custom subagent for endpoint implementation whose frontmatter `skills` field lists the api-conventions skill: the full skill content is injected into the worker's context at startup on every run, so the conventions are guaranteed to be in front of it rather than merely discoverable.
answers.rejected_alternative: Relying on discovery through the Skill tool (or on the main session's loaded guidance): subagents start with fresh context that does not include what the main session loaded, and whether a worker chooses to invoke a discoverable skill is model judgment, which is exactly the failure being observed.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness performs the injection at subagent startup, guaranteeing presence in context; actually following the conventions while implementing remains the model's job.
answers.context_boundary: The worker runs in its own context window; the injected full skill content, Claude's delegation prompt, and CLAUDE.md cross in at startup, and only the implementation report crosses back to the main conversation.
answers.lifecycle: Injection happens at startup of every invocation of that subagent and lasts for the life of that instance; each new delegation re-injects the current skill content.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open silently on misconfiguration: a listed skill that is missing or disabled is skipped with only a debug-log warning, so the worker runs unguarded without anyone being told; skills marked disable-model-invocation cannot be preloaded at all. Injection guarantees presence, not obedience.
answers.version_caveat: The preload does not travel to agent teams: the `skills` (and `mcpServers`) frontmatter fields are not applied when the same subagent definition runs as a teammate, which loads skills from project and user settings instead.

enforcement_owner.quote: The full content of each listed skill is injected into the subagent's context at startup.

lifecycle.quote: Use the `skills` field to inject skill content into a subagent's context at startup.

failure_mode.quote: If a listed skill is missing or disabled, Claude Code skips it and logs a warning to the debug log.

version_caveat.quote: The `skills` and `mcpServers` frontmatter fields in a subagent definition are not applied when that definition runs as a teammate.

answers.primary: A PreToolUse hook matched on Bash, defined in the reporting subagent's frontmatter (the documented db-reader validate-readonly-query pattern) or in settings.json: the script reads the tool call JSON from stdin, inspects tool_input.command for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL keywords, and exits with code 2 to block the command before it executes.
answers.rejected_alternative: Permission deny rules such as Bash(psql *): rules match command prefixes and explicitly cannot match the command's content field, so they cannot distinguish a SELECT from an UPDATE issued through the same database CLI; they would block the whole tool or nothing.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: when the hook exits 2, Claude Code blocks the tool call before execution no matter what the worker attempts, and feeds the stderr message back to the model.
answers.context_boundary: The hook runs as an external shell process outside any context window; it receives the tool call as JSON on stdin, and only its stderr block message crosses into the worker's context as feedback.
answers.lifecycle: Fires on every matching Bash tool call, after Claude creates the tool parameters and before the command runs; frontmatter hooks apply only while that subagent is active and are cleaned up when it finishes, while settings.json hooks apply session-wide including inside subagents.
answers.failure_mode: Fails open on script faults: only exit code 2 blocks, so a validator that crashes with exit 1, is not executable, or whose regex misses obfuscated SQL lets the mutation proceed as a non-blocking error. Only the correct exit-2 path fails closed, so the SQL pattern list must be conservative.
answers.version_caveat: Before v2.1.214, a hook that exited 2 while printing JSON that failed schema validation was treated as a non-blocking error and the action proceeded; also, on Windows the validation script should be written in PowerShell with shell: powershell on the hook entry.

enforcement_owner.quote: The effect depends on the event: `PreToolUse` blocks the tool call, `UserPromptSubmit` rejects the prompt, and so on.

lifecycle.quote: Runs after Claude creates tool parameters and before processing the tool call.

failure_mode.quote: Claude Code treats exit code 1 as a non-blocking error and proceeds with the action, even though 1 is the conventional Unix failure code.

version_caveat.quote: Before v2.1.214, Claude Code treated that combination as a non-blocking error and the action proceeded.

answers.primary: A skill launched by name (/cleanup with disable-model-invocation: true) that sets `disallowed-tools: AskUserQuestion` in its frontmatter: the tool is removed from Claude's available pool while the skill is active, so the routine cannot ask clarifying questions, and the restriction clears automatically when the user sends their next message.
answers.rejected_alternative: A PreToolUse hook that denies AskUserQuestion: equally deterministic, but it stays in force while configured, so restoring the capability on the user's next message would need custom state tracking that the skill field's documented clear-on-next-message lifecycle provides natively.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: disallowed-tools removes the tool from the model's available pool for the active window, so no instruction or mid-task decision can call it; this is a structural removal, not advisory prose.
answers.context_boundary: The skill runs inline in the main conversation: its rendered content enters context on invocation and persists, but the tool removal is a harness-side change to the tool pool rather than anything in the context window.
answers.lifecycle: Applies from the moment the user invokes the skill by name and lasts while the skill is active in that turn; the restriction clears when the user sends their next message, which is exactly the automatic restoration the scenario asks for.
answers.failure_mode: Within its window it fails closed, but the scope is per-turn: if the routine's work continues after the user's next message, the restriction has already cleared unless the skill is re-invoked; and like deny rules the field cannot remove EndConversation while any other tool remains.
answers.version_caveat: If the launch-by-name control uses disable-model-invocation: true, note that as of v2.1.196 that flag also prevents the skill from running when a scheduled task fires with the skill as its prompt.

enforcement_owner.quote: Tools removed from Claude's available pool while this skill is active. Use for autonomous skills that should never call certain tools, such as `AskUserQuestion` for a background loop.

lifecycle.quote: The restriction clears when you send your next message.

failure_mode.quote: Like deny rules, the field can't remove

answers.primary: An agent team: five teammates, each a full independent Claude Code session, spawned for competing hypotheses; they message each other directly through per-agent mailboxes to disprove one another and coordinate through the shared task list with self-claiming, matching the documented competing-hypotheses debate pattern.
answers.rejected_alternative: Parallel subagents: they can run five investigations concurrently, but subagents only report results back to the main agent and never talk to each other, so direct adversarial cross-examination between investigators is structurally impossible.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness owns the coordination substrate (teammate spawning, automatic mailbox delivery, and the shared task list with file-locked claiming); the model, as lead and teammates, owns hypothesis quality and convergence.
answers.context_boundary: Each teammate has its own independent context window that loads project context (CLAUDE.md, MCP servers, skills) plus its spawn prompt; the lead's conversation history does not carry over, and only SendMessage payloads and shared task-list state cross between agents.
answers.lifecycle: The team forms when the first teammate is spawned with the main session as lead; teammates work, message, claim tasks, and go idle, and the team's config directory is cleaned up when the session ends while the task list persists for resumed sessions.
answers.failure_mode: Experimental rough edges rather than enforcement: task status can lag and block dependent tasks, the lead may start implementing or shut down before teammates finish, and /resume does not restore in-process teammates; token cost also scales linearly with teammate count. Nothing fails closed here.
answers.version_caveat: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default; they require setting CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 in settings.json or the environment, and carry documented limitations around resumption, task coordination, and shutdown.

enforcement_owner.quote: Task claiming uses file locking to prevent race conditions when multiple teammates try to claim the same task simultaneously.

lifecycle.quote: An agent team forms when the first teammate is spawned, with the main session acting as the lead.

failure_mode.quote: teammates sometimes fail to mark tasks as completed, which blocks dependent tasks.

version_caveat.quote: Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default. Enable them by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`

answers.primary: Permission deny rules in .claude/settings.json, e.g. "deny": ["Read(vendor/**)"]: Read rules are applied to the built-in reading and searching tools including Grep and Glob, they are enforced by the harness rather than read by the model, and subagents inherit the parent conversation's permission context, so delegated exploration is bound where CLAUDE.md prose is not.
answers.rejected_alternative: Strengthening the CLAUDE.md/rules instruction: it is advisory, and the built-in Explore and Plan research subagents skip CLAUDE.md entirely to keep research cheap, which is precisely why the delegated searches keep touching vendor/ today.
answers.enforcement_owner: The harness: deny rules block the tool call before it is attempted, in the main session and inside every subagent, regardless of what any agent's instructions say.
answers.context_boundary: The rule lives in settings outside any context window and is evaluated on each tool call in both the main session and subagent contexts; only the denial feedback enters the acting agent's context, and the vendor/ contents never do.
answers.lifecycle: Loaded from the settings file and applied to every matching tool call for the life of the session, inherited into subagents as part of the permission context; it stops applying only when removed from settings.
answers.failure_mode: Fails closed for built-in file tools and Bash file commands Claude Code recognizes (cat, head, tail, sed), but fails open for arbitrary subprocesses such as a Python or Node script that opens vendor/ files itself, and the Read-rule coverage of Grep and Glob is documented as best-effort; OS-level enforcement requires the sandbox.
answers.version_caveat: A Read deny rule also blocks the Edit tool on the same path only on v2.1.208 or later, and Write/NotebookEdit are never covered by Read rules, so add an Edit deny rule for paths no tool may change.

enforcement_owner.quote: Permission deny rules block Claude from even attempting to access restricted resources

lifecycle.quote: Subagents inherit the permission context from the main conversation

failure_mode.quote: They don't apply to arbitrary subprocesses that read or write files indirectly, like a Python or Node script that opens files itself.

version_caveat.quote: Write and NotebookEdit aren't covered, so add an `Edit` deny rule for paths no tool may change. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later.
